title: Next-year rangeland fire occurrence in the southern BC/Alberta dry interior
question: Given public earth-observation and biodiversity features known by the end of year t, what is the probability that a 2 km rangeland cell burns by NBAC in year t+1?

region.name: southern BC and southern Alberta dry interior

grid.note: The 2 km Albers rectangle bounding the WGS84 bbox also contains projection-corner cells outside the study area; all corpora are restricted to cell centers inside the WGS84 bbox.

label.name: burned_next_year
label.definition: 1 if the NBAC burn fraction in the 2 km cell in year t+1 is >= 0.01, else 0
label.rasterization: NBAC polygons rasterized at 400 m and block-averaged to 2 km

mask.note: 0.2 was chosen for more training rows; 0.3 also clears the 0.5% gate (0.005683), 0.5 does not (0.003161).

spatial_folds.method: contiguous x-quantile blocks over study cells; balanced by cell count, not fire count
spatial_folds.note: fire occurrence is spatially concentrated; test positives by fold are 270, 135, 0, 0, 0, so by-fold AP is reported only where defined

splits.rule: no test tuning; test evaluated once after model selection

climate.source: Daymet single-pixel API, sampled on a 0.1 degree lattice and bilinearly interpolated to 2 km

modis.source: MODIS MOD13Q1 250 m NDVI/EVI seasonal metrics

invasion.source: GBIF cumulative records for Bromus tectorum, Bromus japonicus, Ventenata dubia, Aegilops cylindrica
invasion.rule: records with year <= t; unknown year treated as 2000

leakage_rules: all features use information available by the end of feature year t
invasion records use year <= t; unknown year defaults to 2000
fire history uses only years <= t
medians and z-score statistics are fit on training rows only
no test-year information is used for feature selection or model selection

preprocessing.scaling: z-score with training mean and standard deviation; constant columns use sd=1
preprocessing.note: oversampling repeats positive training rows; no class weights in the Lancius CE objective

primary.name: lancius_i4_mlp
primary.optimizer: SGD with momentum 0.9 and weight decay 1e-4

calibration.note: test labels are not used; AP and ROC-AUC are invariant

ablations: static + climate + fire_history (no modis, no invasion)

metrics.reporting: mean and 95% bootstrap interval over cells for the temporal test years; no test tuning
metrics.causal_claim: none; this is a predictive risk model, not a causal attribution
metrics.calibration_method: Platt scaling fitted on validation logits, applied to test probabilities

acceptance.model_requirement: met for prevalence and logistic baselines; below LightGBM on test AP; reported honestly without test tuning
acceptance.prevalence_gate: met at rangeland fraction >= 0.2 inside the WGS84 bbox (0.007358)
acceptance.model_result: test AP 0.03668 (95% cell-bootstrap CI 0.03198-0.04327) vs prevalence 0.00698, logistic 0.03445, LightGBM 0.04611; calibrated Brier 0.006832, log-loss 0.035182, ECE 0.002697

limitations: the projected grid rectangle covers cells outside the WGS84 bbox; these are excluded before corpus assembly
fire occurrence is spatially concentrated; three of five provisional spatial folds have no test positives
climate is sampled at roughly 11 km and interpolated to 2 km, not native 1 km
GBIF records are sparse and biased toward accessible/roaded areas
fire history is left-censored at 2013 and capped at 3 years since fire
NBAC labels may miss small or low-intensity fires
spatial folds are provisional until an ecodistrict layer is sourced
no causal interpretation; feature importance is associational
Platt calibration is fit on only 97 validation positives; calibration uncertainty is high
